- Any planned temporary/transient processors (e.g., short windows for edge caches) and their fallback/onshore options.

Can you provide this by EOD CET Thursday (2026-12-17)? If there are known exceptions to EU-only residency, please flag them and include the compensating controls.

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two files: a compact roster (subprocessor_roster_20261214.csv) and a dataflow PDF (dataflow_eu_map_v2.pdf). Summary below:

Quick summary:
- Total subprocessors: 18 (see CSV).
- EU-hosted primary processors: 12.
- Notable transient processors: EdgeRoute Ltd (edge caching, temporary bursts), Cachebound (edge telemetry). Both are used for short-term caching and can be disabled per account.
- Transit note: EdgeRoute performs TCP egress that, for certain European POPs, routes via our US-east transit for stabilization during bursts (~<5% of requests on peak windows). This is used only for caching headers/KV eviction traffic, not raw user content; the CSV flags this as "transit_through_us".

Security and controls:
- All network transit is TLS1.3 (in flight).
- EdgeRoute and Cachebound data at rest use customer-namespace encryption; EdgeRoute supports AES-256 at rest.
- SOC2 link: https://redwood-inference.example.com/audit/soc2 (redacted public report—full report available under NDA).
- KMS: we use customer-managed KMS in our Private deployments and platform-managed KMS for hosted (details in CSV).

Temporary processors and fallback:
- We have an onshore fallback (EU-onshore cache pool) that can be enabled for accounts requiring strict residency. Enabling is a configuration flip and would be completed within 24–72 hours depending on throughput.

Attachments:
- subprocessor_roster_20261214.csv (columns: name | role | country | residency_flag | transit_note | support_contact)
- dataflow_eu_map_v2.pdf (visual map with redlines where transit crosses to non-EU)

If you'd like, Stephanie and I can schedule a short call to walk through the PDF.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Vendor Risk & Onboarding — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the files. A couple of clarifying points before we sign the annex:

1) EdgeRoute transit: your note says routing for bursts may go via US-east for stabilization. Can you confirm whether any PII blobs (message bodies, embeddings) traverse that path, or is it limited to control/eviction metadata?
2) Encryption: please confirm AES-256 at rest applies to any cached content that could include PII, and provide the specific KMS key residency (EU-only or global) used for hosted accounts.

If you can reply with two short bullets on those items, we should be able to finalize. If any of this requires an NDA to view the SOC2 artifact, say so and we will route on our side.

Appreciate it —
Asha Menon
